verses.text: In the twenty-third year of the reign of Joash son of Ahaziah, king of Judah, Jehoahaz son of Jehu became king of Israel. He ruled in Samaria for seventeen years.
He did what was evil in the LORD's sight and followed the sins Jeroboam son of Nebat had led Israel into. He never turned away from them.
The LORD's anger burned against Israel, and he kept handing them over to Hazael king of Syria and to Hazael's son Ben Hadad.
Jehoahaz begged the LORD for help, and the LORD listened to him. He saw how badly the king of Syria was oppressing Israel.
The LORD gave Israel a deliverer, so they escaped Syrian control and lived in their tents again as before.
Even so, they didn't turn from the sins Jeroboam's family had led Israel into. They continued in them, and the Asherah pole still stood in Samaria.
The king of Syria left Jehoahaz only fifty horsemen, ten chariots, and ten thousand foot soldiers. He had destroyed the rest, crushing them like dust at a threshing floor.
The rest of Jehoahaz's acts, everything he did, and the power he showed are recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
Jehoahaz died and joined his ancestors, and they buried him in Samaria. His son Joash became king in his place.
In the thirty-seventh year of King Joash's reign over Judah, Jehoash son of Jehoahaz became king of Israel. He ruled in Samaria for sixteen years.
He did what was evil in the LORD's sight. He kept on committing all the sins Jeroboam son of Nebat had led Israel into.
The rest of Joash's acts, everything he did, and the power he showed fighting King Amaziah of Judah are recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
Joash died and joined his ancestors, and Jeroboam took his throne. Joash was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel.
When Elisha became sick with the illness that would kill him, King Joash of Israel came down to see him. He wept over him and cried, “My father, my father! The chariots of Israel and its horsemen!”
Elisha told him, “Get a bow and arrows.” So he got a bow and arrows.
Elisha said to the king of Israel, “Put your hand on the bow.” He did, and Elisha laid his hands over the king's hands.

“Open the east window,” Elisha said. The king opened it. “Shoot!” Elisha said, and he shot. Elisha said, “The LORD's arrow of victory! The arrow of victory over Syria! You'll strike the Syrians at Aphek until you've finished them.”
Then he said, “Take the arrows.” The king took them. “Strike the ground,” Elisha said, and the king struck it three times and stopped.
The man of God was angry with him. “You should have struck five or six times,” he said. “Then you'd have defeated Syria completely. Now you'll defeat Syria only three times.”
Elisha died and was buried. Moabite raiding bands used to invade the land at the start of the year.

One day some people were burying a man when they saw a band of raiders. They threw the man's body into Elisha's tomb. As soon as the body touched Elisha's bones, the man came back to life and stood up.
Hazael king of Syria oppressed Israel throughout Jehoahaz's reign.
But the LORD was gracious to Israel and had compassion on them because of his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. He wouldn't destroy them, and he had not yet driven them from his presence.
Hazael king of Syria died, and his son Ben Hadad became king in his place.
Jehoash son of Jehoahaz took back from Ben Hadad son of Hazael the towns Ben Hadad had captured from his father Jehoahaz in battle. Joash defeated him three times and recovered the towns of Israel.
